pl-l3d10c3-d1e117.summary: Asks whether the predestination the Apostle mentions concerns the person or the nature, and answers that both can be soundly said: the Son's person, which always was, was predestined according to the man assumed, so that, being man, it would be Son of God; and human nature was predestined to be personally united to the Father's Word.
claims: The Son's person was predestined according to the assumed man.
Human nature was predestined to be united to the Word.

pl-l3d10c3.summary: Asks whether the predestination the Apostle mentions (Rom 1:4) concerns the person or the nature. Both can be said: the Son's person, which always existed, was predestined according to the assumed man, that he, being man, would be Son of God; and human nature was predestined to be personally united to the Father's Word.
claims: The Son's person was predestined according to the assumed humanity.
Human nature was predestined to be personally united to the Word.
